Silence the commitEditing deprecation by declaring the method where it is implemented. The punch list recorded this as a call that needed replacing, which was wrong: commitEditing was not removed, it moved from a deprecated informal category on NSObject in NSKeyValueBinding.h onto the formal NSEditor protocol. Every warning came from a receiver whose own interface never declared the method, so the compiler resolved the call against the old category. Declaring it in the two class extensions that implement it clears all eight. Adopting NSEditor outright looked tempting and also silences them, but it would be a promise neither class can keep, because the protocol requires discardEditing, commitEditingWithDelegate:didCommitSelector:contextInfo: and commitEditingAndReturnError: as well, and neither implements any of the three

Replace the deprecated NSKeyedArchiver and NSKeyedUnarchiver initialisers in the file browser with their modern forms, and report a read failure instead of silently ignoring it. Secure coding is deliberately left off. Turning it on is not a flag flip: restoreStateWithCoder: decodes every value with decodeObjectForKey:, which throws under secure coding because it names no expected classes, and the superclass also writes into this archive, so its contents would have to cooperate too. Nothing in the suite exercises state restoration, and a throw here would quietly lose file browser history and expansion rather than fail visibly, so adopting it properly wants the running app

Replace mktemp with mkstemp, and give the one caller that wanted a directory an mkdtemp of its own. mktemp only reserves a name, so any other process can claim the path in the window before the caller opens it. The file callers all open the result with O_CREAT and O_TRUNC rather than O_EXCL, so finding the file already created changes nothing for them. The test jail was the exception: it called the same function and then made a directory at the returned path, which stops working the moment something real is sitting there. It now goes through a new path::temp_dir that names and creates the directory in one atomic step, which closes the same race on that side. The hanging io_test found this, not the compiler. Also swaps alternateSelectedControlColor for selectedContentBackgroundColor, and the deprecated NSAccessibilityException name for NSRangeException, which is what the throw site actually describes

Update the vendored Onigmo from 5.15.0 to 6.2.0. The fork carried no local commits, so this is a clean fast forward of 585 upstream commits rather than a merge, but Onigmo 6 is not a drop in replacement. It renamed the umbrella header from oniguruma.h to onigmo.h, spelled out the encoding source file names, and moved the generated Unicode tables into a directory it expects on the include path. It also decides the width of st_data_t by comparing SIZEOF_LONG and SIZEOF_LONG_LONG against SIZEOF_VOIDP, and an undefined macro reads as zero, so the hand maintained config.h had to learn the two sizes it never previously needed. This drops the deprecated-non-prototype warnings from 37 to 8, all 8 now in a single vendored hash table implementation. IMPORTANT: the submodule now points at a commit that exists only in the local clone, fetched from k-takata/Onigmo. A recursive clone of this branch will fail until textmate3/Onigmo is pushed forward to 6.2.0

Replace the deprecated NSWorkspace launch calls with the NSWorkspaceOpenConfiguration family. The launch option bit mask becomes properties on a configuration object, so NSWorkspaceLaunchWithoutActivation is now activates set to NO and NSWorkspaceLaunchWithoutAddingToRecents is addsToRecentItems set to NO. The Open With menu loses its AppleScript detour entirely: it built an odoc Apple event by hand purely because, as its own comment said, the old URL based call could not open more than one document at a time, and openURLs:withApplicationAtURL: does exactly that. The mate tool wraps the new call in a semaphore, because the replacement reports through a completion handler on a background queue while the tool goes straight on to talk to the application over its socket

Replace vfork with posix_spawn in the four sites that are actually compiled. vfork borrows the parent address space, so the child may legally do almost nothing before exec, and every one of these children broke that rule. posix_spawn expresses the same setup declaratively: POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT replaces the loop that closed every inherited descriptor, POSIX_SPAWN_SETSIGDEF with an explicit signal set replaces resetting four handlers by hand, and a process group of zero replaces setpgid(0, getpid()). The one place the translation is not exact is the working directory: the forked child ignored a chdir failure, while posix_spawn fails the whole spawn when a file action fails, so the directory change is now requested only when the directory exists. The test suite caught that difference. Exec failure also stops travelling back as a child exit code, since posix_spawn returns the error to the caller directly. OakDebug has a fifth vfork, left alone because no target compiles that framework

Replace every variable length array with a std::vector or a std::string, and remove the two variables that were set but never read. Variable length arrays are a C99 feature that C++ never adopted, so Clang accepts them only as an extension. The ranker keeps its two dimensional matrix[i][j] indexing through a vector of row pointers, which leaves the dozen index sites in the matching walk untouched, at the cost of moving the matrix off the stack. In the privileged tool the unread variable held the return values of bind and listen, checked only by assert, which the release build compiles away. Those are now checked explicitly and the helper exits with a diagnostic if either fails, so a socket that cannot listen no longer looks like a working one

Remove the last of the NSUserNotification code from the crash reporter. The delivery path already went through UNUserNotificationCenter, but the class still declared NSUserNotificationCenterDelegate and kept both of its methods, plus an applicationDidFinishLaunching: hook whose only job was forwarding NSApplicationLaunchUserNotificationKey to one of them. UNUserNotificationCenter delivers a launch-time notification click through didReceiveNotificationResponse: instead, so the hook had nothing left to do. Its removal does not delay delegate registration, because the very next line of the application delegate still touches the shared instance. Replace the deprecated pasteboard type constants with their UniformTypeIdentifiers-era replacements. CHANGELOG: record the FSEvents move to dispatch queues

Move FSEvents streams from run loop scheduling to dispatch queues, replacing the deprecated FSEventStreamScheduleWithRunLoop at all three sites. Callbacks go to the main queue rather than a background one, which preserves existing threading exactly: scm's schedule_update reads CFRunLoopGetCurrent to hop back to and mutates shared state without locking, and the main run loop drains the main queue, so delivery timing is unchanged. The two FSEventStreamFlushSync calls are removed because a synchronous flush cannot be serviced by the queue that is blocked calling it, which would deadlock. Nothing depended on that synchrony: streams start from kFSEventStreamEventIdSinceNow or signal replay completion asynchronously through kFSEventStreamEventFlagHistoryDone. Verified by io_test, whose four watcher tests make real filesystem changes and fail on a five second timeout if callbacks stop arriving
